section_header: REAR AXLE AND SUSPENSION — IRS Type Rear Axle Shaft
title: REAR AXLE AND SUSPENSION — IRS Type Rear Axle Shaft

content.description: Cross-section diagram showing outer race removal from axle housing using a brass bar

content.text: Using a brass bar, remove the axle shaft outer bearing race from the axle housing.

content.description: Illustration showing use of chisel to open clearance between hub and bearing

content.text: 10. REMOVE OUTSIDE BEARING AND OIL SEAL
(a) Using a chisel, open a clearance between the hub and bearing.
Be careful not to damage the bearing or shaft.

content.description: Diagram showing SST tools being used to remove outer bearing from rear axle shaft

content.text: (b) Using SST, remove the outer bearing from the rear axle shaft.
(c) Remove the oil seal from axle shaft.
INSPECTION AND REPLACEMENT OF REAR AXLE SHAFT COMPONENTS

content.description: Illustration showing inspection of rear axle shaft and flange for wear, damage or runout

content.text: 1. INSPECT REAR AXLE SHAFT AND FLANGE FOR WEAR, DAMAGE OR RUNOUT
If the rear axle flange is damaged or worn, or if runout is greater than maximum, replace the rear axle shaft.
2. CLEAN AND INSPECT BEARINGS AND RACES
(a) Clean with solvent and dry with low-pressure compressed air.
(b) Inspect inner and outer bearings and races for wear or damage.
If a bearing or race requires replacement, it must be replaced as a set with the appropriate bearing or race.
